design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — orthodontic_benefits task 1 (Cascade Ortho Rider Family 1500, case OC-72-56930, Joanna Gerrity), rework round 5.

1. Why this is a good test. The caller, herself the patient, asks only to repay what Cascade overpaid on her braces. The scored figure is the repayment. Getting it requires (a) reading out of the repayment rule that the amount is not fixed until the latest establishment entry is a takeover entry whenever the appliances were placed before the waiting period ended, (b) working out from the rider, the dental enrollment and the case that coverage of the case began 2026-07-01 while the braces went on 2026-03-12, (c) re-establishing the case as a takeover under the agreement of the practice now treating her (she moved from the closed Gallagher practice to Hennessey Orthodontics in September), with the months still to come and the recognised covered-treatment fee under six ladders, and (d) computing the repayment on the world after the re-establishment under five ladders.

2. Scope. ortho_ext_waiting_takeover_fee -> allowed_case_fee of record_ortho_takeover_case_574129ed (owner agent, trigger state_due, 6 factors); ortho_ext_member_overpayment_return -> amount of repay_ortho_overpayment_ce1ed3cf (owner user, 5 factors). One value_input edge, state form.

3. Problem tree. Root ortho_ext_member_overpayment_return <- ortho_ext_waiting_takeover_fee via est_fee / est_remaining on the latest establishment entry. Prerequisite sentence: "The amount a member repays on a case is not fixed until the case's latest establishment entry is a takeover entry whenever the case's appliances were placed before its waiting period ended." False at frozen time.

4. Recognised covered-treatment fee. Plain base: adult waiting months 24, no prior-coverage credit. Factors: dental_tenure 6 (Premier 2000 since 2022-07-01, 30 whole months before the rider; dental coverage is never counted as orthodontic coverage) -> net 18, coverage 2026-07-01, months before coverage 3, still to come 23 (2 before the month of the move, 21 from it); start_work_share 15; retention_part 10; practice_records_visit 78.00 (Hennessey's 2026-09-15 D0150 under the agreement on the transfer entry, no pano that day); covered_payment_shape (method): moved case -> months before the move month at the allowed fee 5200.00, the rest at the fee of the practice now treating the patient, the lesser of it and Hennessey's rate 3100.00 / 19 x 26 = 4242.11 (the retention part is valued at that fee by the retention factor); treating_practice_plan: Hennessey plans 19 months where the new-start plan still had 20 -> 19 of the 21 months from the move month counted. (5200.00 x 2 + 4242.1053 x 19) x 75% / 26 + 4242.1053 x 10% - 78.00 = 2971.2105, rounded 2971.21.

5. Repayment. Standard: takeover benefit = the case-benefit clause in force (coinsurance for the network on the takeover entry, unused deductible 50.00, no proration for a superseding takeover, limited to 1500.00), spread over the 8 installments of the original schedule, every payable installment paid in full. Factors: covered_network_terms (method) 49.1304 (2 covered months at Gallagher out of network, 21 at Hennessey in network), progress_records_offset 92.00 (Hennessey's 2026-11-10 D0330, after the move), takeover_retention_reserve 10%, takeover_installment_count 7 (21 months within the cap window), first_period_share 2/3. Benefit 1435.20; less 92.00 = 1343.20; x 90% / 7 = 172.70; payable round(172.70 x 1.6667, 2) = 287.83; paid 656.26; repayment MN(375.00, 368.43) = 368.43.

6. Base invariants. Waiting months, prior-coverage credit, coinsurance for an establishment entry's network and the unused deductible follow the base rules; the restated case-benefit clause states the takeover entry's network, which is the network factor's baseline. Declared overwrites (repayment rule only): payment reversal grounds (restated for every person), takeover proration (restated for every takeover, a superseding takeover not prorated) and the case-benefit sentence; the carried-payment rule retires no benefit-calculation sentence and applies the rider's benefit rule as in force, so no sibling overwrite exists. The takeover entry takes the network status and agreement in force on its date. Lookback: the initial payment is 245 days old (365 allowed).

7. World rows. Member profile; Hennessey practice with its PPO agreement (effective 2015-04-01) and remittances for both records lines; Direct Bill account with every coverage month 2022-07..2026-11 invoiced 20 days before its first day and paid (110.03, plus 12.60 for the rider from 2025-01), and the 2026-12 invoice issued 2026-11-11, not yet due; Premier 2000 enrollments for Joanna and Lena since 2022-07-01; dental lines (Joanna 2023-08-15 D0330 and 2025-11-04 D0120/D0274 at a general dentist, banding-day D0150 at Gallagher without agreement, Hennessey 2026-09-15 D0150 and 2026-11-10 D0330; Lena's banding-day D0150), each within the Premier 2000 evaluation count and panoramic interval; no annual-maximum postings for Premier 2000 preventive lines; the rider; the new-start entry (allowed 5200.00, fee 5600.00) and the 2026-09-25 transfer entry (revised plan 25 months, 19 remaining, fee 3100.00, recognised fee by the transfer rule on that date); initial 375.00 and installments of 140.63 for 2026-06 and 2026-09.

8. Persona. States the adult braces, the dates, the closed practice and the move to Hennessey, the rider and dental start, the checks received; never names a takeover, a re-establishment or an amount.

9. Reachability. Every gold argument is read from a lookup return or the rule text (traces at steps 12 and 14); the agreement is reached by find_provider_agreements(); the practice row is in closure through find_provider_payment_events(customer_id).

10. Standard solution. Identify and verify; read rider, cases, payments, dental plans, lines, billing account and ledger, agreements and the practice ledger; record the takeover (Hennessey agreement, in_network, 23 months, 2971.21); hand the member the repayment against the initial payment (368.43).

11. Verification. Scratch evaluator over check_compute's DSL: 2971.21 and 368.43; all-baseline 3400.00 and 291.10; per-factor baselines differ from gold. Skipping the takeover gives 318.76.

12. Most likely errors. Repaying on the new-start entry; recording the takeover with the new-start entry's network; one coinsurance for months at two practices; ignoring the tenure reduction; counting Gallagher's or Lena's lines as the orthodontist's records; valuing the months after the move at the allowed fee where Hennessey's rate is lower; counting covered months beyond Hennessey's plan; spreading over the 8 original installments; paying the first quarter in full.

13. Revisions (round 5). Carry percentage removed; dental tenure is a parameter with no month-for-month credit; the takeover fee's method follows the payment shape the rider gives the case (lump case, moved case, otherwise) with months before the latest move at the allowed fee for any number of moves; the plan of the practice now treating caps the covered months after the move; the network factor's baseline is the clause in force.
user_scenario:
You are Joanna Gerrity, an office manager at a Yakima accounting firm who likes to keep her paperwork squared away. You are forty-three. You got braces yourself on March 12, 2026 at Gallagher Orthodontics, a practice that was not in Cascade's network, so Cascade has been paying you directly: a start-up payment in March and then checks in June and September. Dr. Gallagher retired and closed the office at the end of August, so since September 15 you have been treated by Dr. Ronan Hennessey at Hennessey Orthodontics, and in September you recorded the change of orthodontist with Cascade yourself. You added the orthodontic rider to your family's Cascade dental plan back in January 2025. Last weekend you reread the rider booklet and saw that adult orthodontic treatment has a waiting period, and you now think your braces went on before your waiting period was over, so Cascade has probably paid you money it should not have. You would rather fix that now than get a letter later. You are calling to find out what you owe back and to pay it back today.

You open by giving your name and saying you think Cascade overpaid you for your braces and you want to pay back whatever is owed. You do not know the amount and you never suggest one; you also do not know how Cascade works it out.

If the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your full name, Joanna Gerrity, and your phone number, 5095550118; if they ask for more, you give your date of birth, 1983-06-30, and your ZIP code, 98902. If they ask for your member ID you read it from your card: CM72077416. If they ask for the braces case number, you read it from the approval letter: OC-72-56930. If they ask about earlier orthodontic coverage, you say you never had any before this rider. If they ask how long the family has had Cascade dental, you say since July 2022. If they ask how many checks you received, you say the start-up payment in March and checks in June and September, and nothing since.

You are happy for the agent to do whatever has to be done on Cascade's side to work out the right figure. When the agent tells you the amount and hands you the step to pay it back, you complete that step yourself with exactly the values the agent gives you and read back the confirmation. When the agent confirms the repayment has been recorded, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.ortho_rider_id: Value e68afc61-7a05-4802-a13e-8b3a41f46b97. Basis: docstring 'the patient's orthodontic rider, as returned by the orthodontic rider lookup for the subscriber'; one rider, Joanna Gerrity's Cascade Ortho Rider Family 1500. Uniqueness: no other rider.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.ortho_case_event_id: Value bf108f98-745c-4c58-8e58-ce0768c2ce0f. Basis: docstring 'the establishment entry being superseded'; find_ortho_cases returns one establishment entry (OC-72-56930, new start) and one transfer entry. Uniqueness: the transfer entry 2ee629c0-2a46-4b1f-8ca1-7006a3db18a5 is not an establishment entry.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.provider_agreement_id: Value 1d597c16-884b-46b5-83e2-25c9a76e47ee. Basis: the slot sentence: the takeover entry 'takes the network status and participation agreement fixed for the practice now treating the patient on the date of the takeover entry'; find_provider_agreements() returns Dr. Ronan Hennessey's Cascade PPO agreement, orthodontist, effective 2015-04-01, also named on the 2026-09-25 transfer entry. Uniqueness: no other agreement names the practice treating Joanna.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.network_status: Value in_network. Basis: an agreement in force with the orthodontist specialty on the date of the takeover entry gives in network. Uniqueness: the new-start entry's out_of_network status belongs to Gallagher on the banding date.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.months_remaining: Value 23. Basis: 'the months of treatment still to come when coverage begins are the planned treatment months on the new-start entry less the months of treatment before coverage': adult waiting 24 less the 6-month tenure reduction = 18, coverage begins 2026-07-01; months before coverage 18 - 14 - 1 = 3; 26 - 3 = 23. Uniqueness: without the tenure reduction 17.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.allowed_case_fee: Value 2971.21. Basis: ortho_ext_waiting_takeover_fee on the frozen state (factor trace at step 12). Uniqueness: every factor sits on one tier; each baseline gives a different value.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value 368.43. Basis: ortho_ext_member_overpayment_return after the step-12 takeover entry (factor trace at step 14). Uniqueness: every factor sits on one tier; the skipped takeover gives 318.76.

edges.condition: For a case whose banding_date precedes the end of its waiting period, the latest ortho_cases row with event_type ortho_case_established for the case has case_origin takeover (with its months_remaining and allowed_case_fee fixed at re-establishment).
edges.policy_source: The amount a member repays on a case is not fixed until the case's latest establishment entry is a takeover entry whenever the case's appliances were placed before its waiting period ended.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Case OC-72-56930 was banded 2026-03-12 while its coverage begins 2026-07-01 (adult 24 months less the 6-month tenure reduction after the 2025-01-01 rider effective date), and its only establishment entry is a new-start entry.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The takeover re-establishment writes an establishment entry dated 2026-11-20 naming the Hennessey agreement, in_network, case_origin takeover, months_remaining 23 and allowed_case_fee 2971.21; it becomes the latest establishment entry, so est_fee = 2971.21 and est_remaining = 23.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: One prerequisite edge and no parallel prerequisite: the takeover entry must be written first because the repayment reads the latest establishment entry; the reverse order evaluates the repayment on the new-start entry and books a different terminal state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the re-establishment leaves the new-start entry as the latest establishment entry (allowed 5200.00, out of network, 26 months remaining, coverage counted from the banding month); the repayment recomputes to 318.76 instead of 368.43, and no takeover entry exists in the terminal state.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario states only the surface goal (find out what is owed and pay it back) and the situation (adult braces banded March 12, 2026, change of orthodontist in September, rider since January 2025, possibly inside the waiting period). It never mentions a takeover, a re-establishment, a recognised fee or any step to sort out first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: repay_ortho_overpayment_ce1ed3cf records the reversal row and reduces lifetime_benefit_paid with whatever values it receives; it never reads the establishment entries. record_ortho_takeover_case_574129ed writes the takeover entry without checking waiting periods, agreements or rider status.

factor_trace: dental_tenure (parameter): Premier 2000 coverage began 2022-07-01, 30 whole months before the 2025-01-01 rider effective date -> long-tenure reduction 6; baseline 0 2426.47.
start_work_share (parameter): fixed braces -> braces start share 15; baseline 0 3496.21.
retention_part (parameter): fixed braces -> braces retention share 10, valued at the fee of the practice now treating the patient (4242.11); baseline 0 2897.0.

practice_records_visit (parameter, cross_difficulty dental): the latest transfer entry names the Hennessey agreement; its latest paid D0150 under that agreement is 2026-09-15 (allowed 78.00) with no D0330 that day -> 78.00 taken off; the Gallagher banding-day line and Lena's line carry no agreement, the 2026-11-10 D0330 is another date; baseline 0 3049.21.

covered_payment_shape (method): 26 planned months (more than the 6 lump-sum months), one move -> covered months before the month of the move (2026-07 and 2026-08) at the allowed fee 5200.00, the rest at the fee of the practice now treating the patient, the lesser of 5200.00 and Hennessey's rate 3100.00 / 19 x 26 = 4242.11; baseline (every covered month at 5200.00, the retention part still at the fee of the practice now treating) would give 3496.21.

treating_practice_plan (parameter): Hennessey's 19 months remaining are fewer than the 20 the new-start plan still had after the move (26 - MONTHS(2026-03-12, 2026-09-25) = 26 - 6) -> covered months from the month of the move counted up to 19 (of 21); baseline (no cap) 3215.95.

plain: waiting months 24 (adult rider, individual market); credit 0; net 24 - 0 - 6 = 18; months before coverage 18 - MONTHS(2025-01-01, 2026-03-12) - 1 = 18 - 14 - 1 = 3; still to come 26 - 3 = 23 (2 before the move month, 21 from it).

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the attached dental enrollment's coverage began 24 or more whole months before the rider effective date
the latest transfer entry names an agreement AND that practice's records visit has only the D0150 line
the latest transfer entry's months remaining are fewer than the months the new-start plan still had after the move

factor_trace: covered_network_terms (method): Family 1500 coinsurances differ; superseding takeover; moved on 2026-09-25 (month index 6, coverage index 4, before the takeover date) from the out-of-network new-start entry to the in-network transfer entry -> (40 x 2 + 50 x 21) / 23 = 49.1304; baseline (in-network 50 for the takeover entry, as the case-benefit clause states) would give 362.99.

progress_records_offset (parameter, cross_difficulty dental): under the takeover entry's Hennessey agreement the latest paid D0330 is 2026-11-10 (index 8 >= 4, after the 2026-09-25 transfer; plan paid 92.00); the latest D0150 (2026-09-15) is before the transfer -> 92.00 comes off; baseline 0 would give 348.71.
takeover_retention_reserve (parameter): fixed braces -> 10; baseline 0 would give 336.44.
takeover_installment_count (method): quarterly, 23 months remaining > 6, within the cap 24 - (26 - 23) = 21 -> ceil(21/3) = 7; baseline original count ceil(MN(25, 24)/3) = 8 would give 375.0.
first_period_share (parameter): coverage index 26 - 23 + 1 = 4 (2026-07), the second month of the quarter starting at index 3 (2026-06) -> two thirds; baseline all of it would give 310.86.

takeover benefit = MN(round(49.1304 x (2971.21 - 50.00) / 100, 2), 1500.00 - 0.00) = 1435.20 (superseding takeover: no proration); less 92.00 = 1343.20; installment = round(1343.20 x 90% / 7, 2) = round(172.6971, 2) = 172.70.

payable to date: now index MONTHS(2025-01-01, 2026-11-20) - 14 = 8; periods begun at indexes 3 and 6 -> 2 (cap 7); round(172.70 x (2 - 1 + 2/3), 2) = round(287.8333, 2) = 287.83; paid on the case 375.00 + 2 x 140.63 = 656.26.
result = round(MN(375.00, MX(0, 656.26 - 287.83)), 2) = 368.43; all factors at baseline: 291.1.
